name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,329

clue.text: Well-turned-out fir tree (6)

blocks.note: well-turned-out = neat and smart in appearance
a conifer closely related to the fir

annotation.surface: A description of a neatly shaped Christmas tree.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface runs the two senses together as one tree; split it after 'Well-turned-out' and each half defines the answer alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Spruce means smartly dressed, and a spruce is a fir-like evergreen.

clue.text: Where to find aquatic mammal mainly (3)

definitions.text: Where to find aquatic mammal mainly

indicators.note: the main part of the word, not all of it: drop the last letter

blocks.note: the aquatic mammal SEAL without its last letter

annotation.surface: A nature question: where you would go to spot a marine mammal.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the sea is mainly where you find a seal, and most of SEAL is SEA.
annotation.definitionFit: The sea is the home of the seal and other marine mammals.

clue.text: Symbolic items regarding festivity involving capital of Italy (7)

indicators.note: the festivity takes in, or involves, the next letter
the capital letter, the first, of Italy

blocks.note: re = regarding, as in memo headers
a gala is a festive occasion
first letter of Italy, set inside GALA to make GAL(I)A

annotation.surface: Ceremonial trappings on show at a Roman festival.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Italy' looks like Rome; here it is only the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: Regalia are the emblems of royalty or office, such as crowns and sceptres.

clue.text: MPs angry over booze found around northern church (5,8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'over' puts the first piece above the next
BEERS is placed around the other letters

blocks.note: beers = drinks, booze; split around the next letters as BE…ERS

annotation.surface: Furious members of parliament at a bar near a church in the north.
annotation.walkthrough: Crossbenchers sit in the British parliament without party allegiance, on the benches crossways to the rest; the surface's angry MPs are a picture, not the definition's sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Crossbenchers are independent members of the British parliament, sitting on the cross benches.

clue.text: Burning a book ahead of rest (6)

indicators.note: puts A and B in front of the next piece

annotation.surface: Setting fire to a book before taking a break.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests book-burning; the book is only the letter B.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something ablaze is alight with flames.

clue.text: Going by the bar, getting drunk’s origin story? (3,4,6)

indicators.note: drunk letters are tipsy and scrambled

annotation.surface: Someone passing a pub, getting drunk, and telling how it all began.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Origin story' is the definition with a wink: the Big Bang theory is the story of the universe's origin, and the question mark flags the playful phrasing.
annotation.definitionFit: The Big Bang theory is the scientific account of how the universe began.

clue.text: Liberal put in excellent assertion of innocence (5)

indicators.note: LIB is placed inside the other piece

blocks.note: A1 = excellent, first-rate; the 1 is read as the letter I; split around the next piece as A…I

annotation.surface: A Liberal politician placed in a fine plea of innocence.
annotation.walkthrough: A1 turning into AI, with the digit 1 standing for the letter I, is a common crossword trick.
annotation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim that you were elsewhere when the crime happened, so could not be guilty.

clue.text: Success at golf: finally one may be considered keen (5,4)

indicators.note: places the second piece at the end

blocks.note: an eagle is two under par on a hole

annotation.surface: A golfer after a long wait finally has a good hole to reflect on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Keen' here means sharp-sighted, as in keen eyes, not eager.
annotation.definitionFit: Eagle-eyed means having keen, sharp sight.

clue.text: Threatening behaviour in the past limiting King George (5)

indicators.note: AGO sets the limits, on both sides, of GR

blocks.note: ago = in the past; split around the next piece as AG…O

annotation.surface: A history note about bullying that once hemmed in King George.
annotation.walkthrough: GR, Georgius Rex, is the royal cipher of the Georges. Aggro is British slang for aggressive trouble-making.
annotation.definitionFit: Aggro is informal British for aggressive, intimidating behaviour.

clue.text: Drinking, losing head, embracing (7)

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: CHUGGING = drinking fast, without its first letter C

annotation.surface: A drinker losing their head and getting affectionate.
annotation.walkthrough: To chug is to gulp a drink down; behead CHUGGING to leave HUGGING.
annotation.definitionFit: Hugging and embracing both mean holding someone in your arms.

clue.text: House cartoon father left unfinished (4)

indicators.note: the last letter is not included

blocks.note: the father in The Simpsons, cut short by one letter at the end

annotation.surface: A cartoon dad walking out and leaving the house half built.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like the direction or the verb 'departed'; it only belongs to 'left unfinished'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the dwelling where a family lives, used interchangeably with house.

clue.text: Bird of prey seen in low light (3)

indicators.note: the answer is visible inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words, from the end of 'low' into the start of 'light'

annotation.surface: An owl spotted at dusk.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer really does belong in the scene: owls hunt at dusk, in low light.
annotation.definitionFit: Owls are nocturnal birds of prey.

clue.text: Old description of fruit shortage? Not entirely (3,2,4)

indicators.note: the phrase is not given in full: its last letter goes

blocks.clueFragment: description of fruit shortage? Not entirely
blocks.note: a shop with no dates of the palm fruit has run out of them; drop the final S of that phrase

annotation.surface: A dated way of saying the shop has no fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading of 'out of dates' as having run out of the fruit.
annotation.definitionFit: Out of date means old-fashioned or expired.

clue.text: To recap, total is invested in horse (9)

indicators.note: IS is put inside, as money is put into a business

blocks.note: a mare is a female horse; split around the next piece as MAR…E

annotation.surface: A financial summary: the total sum has gone into a racehorse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Invested' pulls toward money, fitting 'total'; it is the container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean going back over the main points briefly.

clue.text: French composer on time for journey (6)

indicators.note: in an across clue, RAVEL goes on, after, T

annotation.surface: A French composer arriving punctually for a trip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On time' reads as punctual; it is RAVEL placed after T.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: journey as a verb means to go from place to place, just as travel does.

clue.text: Medium period of time at clubs in US city (6)

indicators.note: being in a city means being inside it, so the clubs letter goes inside the city's letters

blocks.note: an age = a period of time
NY = New York; split around the next piece as N…Y

annotation.surface: A psychic medium spending a while at nightclubs in an American city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Medium' suggests a psychic; here it means a means or channel, as in 'through the agency of'.
annotation.definitionFit: An agency is a medium through which something is done.

clue.text: Seat now broken? Don’t worry about it (2,5)

indicators.note: the letters are broken apart and rebuilt

annotation.surface: Someone apologising for breaking a chair and being told it is fine.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a complete exchange: the chair breaks and the host shrugs it off with the answer itself.
annotation.definitionFit: No sweat is an informal way of saying don't worry, it's no trouble.

clue.text: Young guy involving daughter in organisation (4)

indicators.note: to involve is to include or take in, so the young guy takes the daughter's letter inside him

blocks.note: a boy is a young male; split around the next piece as BO…Y

annotation.surface: A young man getting his daughter into some organisation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Organisation' is the definition in its sense of an organised group, as in 'a professional body'.
annotation.definitionFit: A body is an organised group, as in a governing body.

clue.text: Confront the clergy? It helps to have a clean look (4,5)

definitions.text: It helps to have a clean look

blocks.note: 'the cloth' = the clergy, as in 'a man of the cloth'

annotation.surface: Standing up to the church, then tidying yourself up.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a face cloth helps your face look clean.
annotation.definitionFit: A face cloth is a small towel for washing your face.

clue.text: Firm outer covering yielding last source of powder (5)

indicators.note: to yield is to give up or surrender, so the covering surrenders its last letter

blocks.note: COAT without its last letter T

annotation.surface: A hard shell giving up the last of some powder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective describing the covering; it is the noun, a company.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by function: the seeds of the cacao tree are roasted and ground into the brown powder used for drinks and baking.

clue.text: Blue stand, with regular pieces missing (3)

indicators.note: every other letter is taken out

annotation.surface: A broken blue stand missing some parts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like a colour describing the stand; it means unhappy.
annotation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means feeling sad.

clue.text: Aluminium, carbon and helium linked to my former quest for gold? (7)

indicators.note: joins MY on after the chemical symbols

annotation.surface: A list of elements joined to the old dream of making gold.
annotation.walkthrough: The chemical elements in the wordplay suit the answer, the forerunner of chemistry that sought to turn base metals into gold.
annotation.definitionFit: Alchemy was the medieval pursuit of turning base metals into gold.

clue.text: Stage production to start without new artist (5)

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the word for 'start' goes on lacking the letter for 'new'

blocks.note: OPEN = to start, without N for new

annotation.surface: A show being staged without a new painter.
annotation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts, is the usual crossword artist.
annotation.definitionFit: An opera is a musical drama staged in a theatre.

clue.text: Manner reasonable, but not fine (3)

indicators.note: 'but not' excludes something, so the word for reasonable keeps everything except the letter for fine

blocks.note: FAIR = reasonable, without F for fine

annotation.surface: A verdict on someone's manner: reasonable, but no better.
annotation.walkthrough: F = fine, as marked on pencils and grades.
annotation.definitionFit: An air is a manner or bearing, as in 'an air of confidence'.

clue.text: Pass drinks in middle of speech (6)

indicators.note: drinks served in the middle of a speech sit within it, so the drinks' letters go inside
the central letters of the word

blocks.note: the middle two letters of spEEch; split around the next piece as E…E
laps = drinks, as a cat laps milk

annotation.surface: Handing round drinks halfway through a speech.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pass' could be the verb 'hand round'; here it is time passing.
annotation.definitionFit: Time elapses, meaning it passes.

clue.text: Bizarre story about European shellfish (6)

indicators.note: the letters of story are bizarrely rearranged
the rearranged letters go around E

blocks.note: anagram of STORY; split around the next piece as OYST…R

annotation.surface: A strange tale told about a European seafood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Story' looks like part of the tale in the surface; it is only the letters to be rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the oyster is one kind of shellfish, a bivalve prized for eating and for pearls.
